instrument.state: An item or record passes through multiple handlers or locations, creating opportunities for substitution, alteration, contamination, or uncertainty about identity.
instrument.operation: Record each transfer and handling event with the responsible party, time, and purpose, then inspect that history for continuity and unexplained transitions.
instrument.signal: A continuous, internally consistent handling record links the examined item through its lifecycle, while gaps or contradictions identify breaks in documented custody.
instrument.inference: Documentary continuity supports the claim that the item examined is the item collected and that its handling history is accounted for; gaps weaken that provenance claim.
instrument.limit: Complete documentation does not itself prove that handlers recorded events truthfully or that no unrecorded alteration occurred, and missing records do not prove that alteration occurred. The strength of the inference depends on the reliability of the recording and safeguarding process.

target.question: What assembly sequence constraints for the opening and closing sections of draft D-17 are justified by its witnessed handling records?

mapping.state: The focal object is novel draft D-17. Two identified sections have contemporaneous witnessed handling records. The inquiry concerns assembly order for the opening and closing sections. Witnesses and safeguarding are reliable for the recorded events; no complete composition record is stipulated.
mapping.operation: Assign stable identifiers to each section, record transfers and witnessed assembly with responsible party, time and purpose, and audit continuity and unexplained transitions. Keep witnessed assembly distinct from inferred composition. Use a warranted opening-section order to constrain the draft reconstruction. Use a warranted closing-section order to constrain the draft reconstruction.
mapping.signal: The opening-section chain is continuous and documents its witnessed attachment before the binding event. The closing-section chain is continuous and documents its witnessed replacement after editorial review. Identifiers persist through both recorded chains without an unexplained transition.
mapping.inference:
The continuous handling histories support identifying the witnessed opening attachment and closing replacement as events involving the corresponding sections of draft D-17.
If the preceding joint conclusion is warranted, the opening-section record supports placing its witnessed attachment before the recorded binding when constraining the assembly sequence of the surviving draft D-17.
If the preceding joint conclusion is warranted, the closing-section record supports placing its witnessed replacement after editorial review when constraining the assembly sequence of the surviving draft D-17.
The continuous handling histories establish that one archive staff member used the same record-entry terminal for the opening attachment and closing replacement in draft D-17.
mapping.limit: All stated recording and safeguarding conditions hold for witnessed events. Documentation does not establish unrecorded composition or exclude every unrecorded revision. No information about the archive staff member’s login or record-entry terminal is supplied.
